\chapter{Appendix}

\section{Notation}
\begin{itemize}
\item Sets are usually denoted with capital letters, e.g., $A,B,C,\dots$
etc; and elements in sets are usually denoted with lowercase letters
$a,b,c,\dots$.
\item If $a$ is an elment in the set $A$, we write $a\in A$. If $a$
is not in $A$ we write $a\notin A$ (slashes usually mean negation). 
\item A set with no elements is called the \emph{empty set}, denoted $\emptyset$.
\item $\mathbb{R}$ the set of all real numbers.
\item $\mathbb{C}$ the set of all complex numbers.
\item $\mathbb{Z}$ the set of all integers.
\item $\mathbb{Q}$ the set of all rational numbers.
\item $\mathbb{N}$ the set of natural numbers.
\end{itemize}
